sealed_candidate.answer: ## Which productivity outcome and comparison should drive the decision (q1 / o1: **unresolved** with declared design only, not a verdict on productivity itself), because per the supplied policy the outcome must be evaluated with **matched tasks under quality gates**, tracking **human review time, rework, elapsed lead time, and total cost**, with **failed or abandoned tasks counted**. The policy explicitly forbids inferring causal benefit from accepted-PR counts (measurement-policy). No productivity verdict can be drawn: the only performance datum is a pilot note reporting 40 accepted PRs in one month, which omits task mix, a control group, reviewer hours, failure counts, and provider costs (measurement-context). The comparison is therefore defined but not yet populated with data.

claims.text: The outcome set is defined by the policy: matched tasks with quality gates, human review time, rework, elapsed lead time, total cost, and counted failed or abandoned tasks; accepted-PR counts must not be used to infer causal benefit.
claims.uncertainty: No material uncertainty; policy is the stated accounting boundary.
